source_title: Patrick Stewart Said He Couldn’t Imagine Ever Retiring from Acting 3 Months Before His Death - People.com
source_excerpt:
The legendary actor, who died at age 86 on Oct. 28, reflected on his future in Hollywood during a July interview with ‘TV Insider’
Patrick Stewart opened up about his future in Hollywood during a July 2026 interview with TV Insider , three months before his death
The Star Trek actor said he couldn’t imagine officially retiring and would “always and forever be an actor”
Stewart, who died on Oct. 28 at age 86, previously shared his thoughts on stepping away from acting in a 2022 interview with PEOPLE
Patrick Stewart had no plans to officially retire from acting before his death.
The legendary actor, who died on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at age 86 , reflected on his decades-long career and his future in Hollywood during a July 2026 interview with TV Insider , just three months before his death.
Stewart, who was best known for portraying Captain Jean-Luc Picard in the Star Trek franchise and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, made it clear that his passion for performing hadn’t faded with age.
“As any actor my age will tell you, there are fewer and fewer available roles as we get older,” Stewart told the outlet when asked whether he was considering retirement or becoming more selective about his projects.
“That being said, I still continue to receive interesting offers and I love being challenged by new work, like voicing a pig’s head in Riz Ahmed’s brilliant new series Bait ,” he continued.
The actor, who turned 86 on July 13, added, “I can’t imagine ever officially ‘retiring.’ I’ll always and forever be an actor.”
At the time, Stewart was also preparing to reprise his role as Professor X in Avengers: Doomsday .
During the same interview, Stewart reflected on the lasting impact of Star Trek , including the franchise’s 60th anniversary and the upcoming 40th anniversary of Star Trek: The Next Generation .
“All of these anniversaries are wildly surreal for me, but the 40th anniversary of The Next Generation is particularly remarkable,” he told TV Insider . “I still remember my first day driving onto the Paramount lot like it was yesterday.”
Although Stewart had returned to his iconic role several times throughout his career, he expressed satisfaction with how his character’s story concluded in Star Trek: Picard , which ended in 2023.
“The final scene of The Next Generation [the episode ‘All Good Things…’] has always felt like such a beautiful send-off, but of course we then filmed multiple movies after the series wrapped,” he explained. “I truly thought Nemesis was my last time playing Jean-Luc, but then along came Picard — and I’m delighted with how that series ended.”
Looking back on the role that transformed his career, Stewart acknowledged just how much the character had come to mean to him.
“Without question, Jean-Luc is the most significant role of my career,” he told the outlet. “And I will be forever grateful to have had the opportunity to be a part of what is now such a historic franchise.”
Stewart had previously opened up about his complicated relationship with retirement in a 2022 interview with PEOPLE.
At the time, the actor admitted that he had once expected to step away from Hollywood much earlier.
“I thought I’d be retired [by now],” he told PEOPLE. “It just hasn’t happened.”
Globe Photos/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock
Stewart also shared that he and his wife, singer Sunny Ozell, had discussed eventually taking time away from their busy lives.
“I’m looking forward to it very much,” he said of the possibility of slowing down. “Although, my wife believes I’ll tolerate it for about two weeks. Then I’ll be calling my agent.”
Despite contemplating the idea, Stewart acknowledged that he wasn’t quite ready to leave performing behind.
“I used to think somebody will have to drag me off the stage or away from the cameras, but I see the little signs that will lead me there at some point,” he told PEOPLE.
“But I’m going to hang in as long as it makes sense,” he added.
Stewart’s determination to continue acting followed a career that spanned more than six decades.
While reflecting on his unexpected success during his 2022 conversation with PEOPLE, Stewart said he was grateful for the opportunities that had come his way.
“There is not a corner of my life that wasn’t impacted,” he said of his breakthrough role on Star Trek .
Stewart died at his Los Angeles home following a battle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, his longtime spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak confirmed in a statement on Thursday, Oct. 29.
“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement read.
“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” the statement continued.
“We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”
